API keys are stored encrypted using Android Keystore secure storage and the AES-256 algorithm. This protects them while stored on the device and prevents extracting keys from persistent storage dumps, such as database files. However, rooted or compromised devices still carry a risk of data compromise, including while data is processed in RAM.

— This section contains profile sign-in and cloud sync.\n— Sign-in opens authentication by email+password or by Google.\n— The sync controls below decide how local and cloud state are combined and which categories are included.

— This section contains backup export and import.\n— Export writes only the selected categories into a JSON backup file.\n— Import reads that backup and separately decides whether local data should be merged or replaced.

— This section defines how the app builds summaries and how it prepares text before AI processing.\n— It also contains text limits, the extra prompt, and adaptive pre-compression rules.\n— Deduplication is configured here too because it uses the same embeddings and similarity thresholds.

— This section stores AI configs for two task types: summary generation and embeddings.\n— Config order decides which provider and model the app tries first.\n— Disabled configs stay in the list but are skipped during requests.

— This section controls the “Recommended” badges on the subscriptions screen in Sources.\n— A theme becomes recommended when important news from your sources is similar to that theme’s anchors.\n— The theme list itself stays visible; only recommendation markers change.

— This section defines how the feed renders cards, filters weaker news, and groups similar items into clusters.\n— Some options affect only card appearance, while others affect the actual set of visible items.\n— Deduplication, similarity thresholds, and minimum match count decide which stories stay separate and which are grouped.

— This section defines automatic summary generation by schedule.\n— A schedule can contain one or several run times per day.\n— Notifications and the size of the statistics block are controlled separately.

— This section defines interface language, summary language, and theme.\n— Interface language affects the whole app, while summary language affects only AI-generated text.\n— Theme affects only how screens look.

— This section contains actions for local data: auto-cleanup, article cleanup, embedding cleanup, summary-history cleanup, and settings reset.\n— Some actions remove only cache-like data, while others restore default behavior.\n— Sources and AI configs are not removed by every action equally, so details are explained below.

— This button opens the AI dialog for the current filtered feed.\n— The selection includes only representative news items that remain after your filters and deduplication.\n— Inside it, you can ask questions about the feed or regenerate the response without going to settings.

— Feed search works across the news title and content.\n— The query is tokenized with debounce, and matching is checked before clusters are built.\n— In “Saved” mode this search is not applied; that mode shows all favorited news that already passed the other filters.

— PDF export saves exactly the current filtered feed.\n— The file includes representative articles from visible clusters, not the full list of duplicates inside them.\n— Media is included or not depending on the “Show media in feed” setting.

— The date filter removes news by `publishedAt` before the final feed is built.
— “Saved” switches the feed to bookmarked news.
— Group selection keeps only sources from that group.
— All of these conditions are applied to the current feed build together with deduplication and the informativeness filter.
— This area shows the feed processing state.\n— The app is grouping similar news and removing duplicates.\n— When processing finishes, the final card list appears here.
— An empty feed means no news matches the current filters.\n— The reason may be date, group, or saved-only mode.\n— Try refreshing sources or relaxing the filters.

— This is a representative news card or a cluster of similar news.\n— If duplicates were found, they are shown inside the card as a separate list with similarity information.\n— The card actions handle opening the source, saving, and AI explanation for a single news item or the whole cluster.

— The “Custom” tab stores your own groups and sources.\n— The “Presets” tab shows the public catalog of ready-made themes.\n— Subscribing from a preset creates a separate group in your custom sources list.

— Search works in the “Custom” tab across group names and source names.\n— The query is split into separate words, and a match requires about 60% of tokens with length of at least 2 characters.\n— If a group name matches, the whole group is shown; if only sources match, the group remains with only the matched items inside.
— Sorting applies to the group list in the “Custom” tab.\n— “Name” orders groups alphabetically.\n— “Date added” places newer groups above older ones.

— This button creates a local group for your own RSS, Telegram, and YouTube sources.\n— The group name must be unique among your groups and reserved subscription names.\n— After creation, you can add sources manually and enable or disable the group separately in the feed.

— This area contains all your source groups and the sources inside them.\n— A group or an individual source can be disabled; then it does not take part in feed refreshes or summaries.\n— Groups created from presets also appear here, but as regular subscriptions linked to the public catalog.

— This area shows themes from the public subscriptions catalog.\n— When you enable a theme, its sources are added as a separate group linked by subscription ID.\n— If recommendations are enabled, badges are calculated by comparing important articles from your sources with theme “anchors” through embeddings; the local or cloud mode is inherited from the deduplication setting.

— This button force-refreshes the public theme catalog and rechecks subscription state.\n— If recommendations are enabled, it also recalculates similarity between your sources and theme “anchors”.\n— If recommendations are disabled, refresh still pulls the current theme list without recalculating recommendation badges.
3. Name: enter it manually or tap “Fetch” to fill it automatically.

2. URL: — Telegram: name, @name, t.me/name, t.me/s/name, https://t.me/name, or www.t.me/name.\n— YouTube: channel ID that starts with UC.\n— RSS: website/feed domain or URL, for example site.com or https://site.com/rss.
1. Source type controls how the parser reads content (RSS/Telegram/YouTube).
4. Subscriptions are organized into folders (groups), so they can be enabled and filtered separately.

— The “Scheduled” tab shows the latest summary and schedule status.\n— The “Statistics” tab builds a ranking of news from the current feed.\n— Both tabs work on data that has already been generated or prepared in the feed.

— This area shows the time of the latest generated summary and the next scheduled time.\n— The next time is calculated from the active scheduled times list and moved to the next day if today’s slot has already passed.\n— This block does not trigger generation by itself; it only shows schedule state.

— This area opens the latest generated summary from the database.\n— It contains the ready text, model name, creation time, and actions for opening sources, saving, or deleting.\n— If no summaries have been generated yet, the block does not appear.

— These switches change the metric for the news ranking in the “Statistics” tab.\n— “Views” uses view count, “Similar” uses cluster size, and “Factuality” uses the factuality score of the news.\n— Switching does not rebuild the feed; it only changes how already prepared data is displayed.

— This area shows the top news items for the selected metric.\n— The data is built from the feed after clustering: a representative news item or an aggregated cluster metric is used.\n— Tapping a card opens the related source if a URL exists for it.

— This button opens the history of previously generated summaries.\n— The list stores records from the database, not newly generated text.\n— Inside history you get search, filters, PDF export, selection, and deletion actions.

— Search in history works across the full text of saved summaries.\n— Matching currently uses a simple `contains(ignoreCase)` check without separate tokenization.\n— It is applied together with the date and favorites filters.

— PDF export saves exactly the list of summaries that remains after the current history filters.\n— The file contains ready history records, not regenerated content.\n— The file name is built from the device’s current date.

— The date filter removes history records by `createdAt` in hours or days.\n— The “Favorites” filter keeps only summaries marked as favorite.\n— These conditions are applied together with search to the saved history.

— A card shows a short preview of a previously generated summary.\n— A normal tap opens the full record, and a long press enables selection mode.\n— The card also provides actions for adding to favorites and deleting the specific record.
— This button scrolls the history list back to the top.\n— It appears only after you scroll down.\n— It does not affect the filters or the history content itself.
— This block opens sign-in or registration.\n— Two sign-in methods are available: email+password and Google.

— This block controls how data is synchronized between devices through Firebase.\n— Below, you choose the interval, included categories, and manual sync actions.\n— API keys require a separate encryption passphrase.
— This block selects what goes into the backup file.\n— It affects JSON backup export only, not automatic sync.\n— API keys can be included only after an encryption passphrase is configured.
— This block selects what to read from a JSON backup file and how to apply it locally.\n— You can merge data or overwrite the local state.\n— API keys require the encryption passphrase.

— This is the passphrase the app uses to derive the encryption key for API keys in sync, backup, and import through PBKDF2.\n— API keys are stored in the file or in Firebase only in encrypted form through AES-256-GCM.\n— On another device, you need the same passphrase again or those API keys cannot be decrypted.

— Cloud sync has 2 modes.\n— `Merge`: if Firebase has newer state, the app pulls it first and then, for each selected category, keeps everything that exists either locally or in the cloud.\n— `Overwrite`: there is no item-by-item merge; after sync only the local side or only the cloud side remains, depending on the priority below.

— This choice matters only in `Overwrite` mode.\n— `Local`: Firebase is replaced with the current state of this device.\n— `Cloud`: this device first accepts the state from Firebase and then continues from that state.

— Only the checked categories take part in sync.\n— `API keys` follow a separate rule: they are written into the JSON backup stored in Firebase only in encrypted form and only if the passphrase above is configured.
— Only the checked categories are written into the backup file.\n— `API keys` are added as a separate JSON block and only in encrypted form if the encryption passphrase is configured.

— Import applies only the categories checked here.\n— Unchecked local data stays unchanged.\n— If the file contains `API keys`, the same encryption passphrase is required to restore them and decrypt the `aiConfigs` block.

— This control decides how backup data is applied locally.\n— `Merge`: for each selected category, everything that exists either locally or in the file is kept.\n— `Overwrite`: selected local categories are fully replaced by the contents of the backup file.
— Changes the language of the whole app interface.\n— This affects menus, buttons, dialogs, and help text.
— Defines which language AI should use for summaries and related answers.\n— It does not change the interface language.
— Controls the visual appearance of the app.\n— You can follow the system theme or force light/dark mode.
— This is the language of the whole app interface.\n— After switching, menus, buttons, dialogs, and help text change on every screen.\n— It does not affect the language of AI summaries.

— This is the language used for summary text and related AI answers.\n— In Ukrainian mode, source meaning is translated but proper names stay unchanged.\n— In English mode, the whole result is produced in English; the app interface language does not change.
— `System`: the app follows the current device theme.\n— `Light` and `Dark`: the app stays in the selected mode regardless of the system setting.\n— This affects only screen appearance.

— This block stores keys, providers, and models used for summary generation.
— The top enabled config is used first.
— Use the arrows to change config order.
— Disabled configurations are ignored during LLM requests.

— This block manages models used for embeddings and similarity-related tasks.\n— These embedding configs are used for cloud deduplication, topic recommendations, and related vector workflows.\n— The top enabled config is used first, and disabled ones are ignored during vectorization.

— This button opens a separate window with direct links to provider pages where API keys are created.\n— After that, sign in to the selected provider account, generate a key there, and paste it into an AI config below.\n— The app does not generate keys itself: it only stores and uses access that the provider already issued.
— This selects the overall summary mode: local, cloud, or adaptive.\n— It affects quality, speed, and token usage.

— The app has 3 summary strategies. `Local`: fully extractive, with no external LLM; top sentences are selected and near-duplicates are filtered by local embeddings.\n— `Cloud`: the app sends a prepared prompt plus trimmed text to one of the enabled summary configs, and if the first config fails it tries the next ones.\n— `Adaptive`: short texts may stay fully local, while longer ones are first extractively compressed by the ranges below and only then sent to the cloud; if there are no active keys or all models fail, the app falls back to local summary.

— Limit for a specific single news item caps cloud text for one-news summaries.
— Limit for a specific news cluster caps total cloud text across all news in a comparison.
— Limit for a single news item in scheduled/full-feed summaries caps one item in cloud digests.
— Limit for a cluster in scheduled/full-feed summaries caps total cluster text when cluster payloads are used.
— Total character limit for sending caps the total payload of one cloud request.
— Lower values speed requests up, but they may cut useful context.

— Local deduplication compares news without a cloud call.\n— Cloud deduplication relies on external AI processing.\n— Adaptive deduplication switches between those approaches depending on available context and runtime conditions.

— The switch enables your own prompt instead of the default template.\n— The text field lets you refine the style or structure of the summary.\n— A custom prompt is an extra instruction, but it does not replace the technical output format rules.

— The first range covers articles up to the lower threshold and uses extractive summarization only.
— The second range covers articles between the lower and upper thresholds.
— The third range covers articles longer than the upper threshold; it has no separate range slider because it means everything above the second threshold.
— Percentages define how much of the sentence set is kept before cloud processing.

— Show media enables images and previews in feed cards.
— Show description adds a text preview below the headline.
— Use full text for feed summary expands the context available for AI summarization.
— Informativeness removes low-score news before display.
— Deduplication groups similar news into clusters, and the thresholds plus minimum match count decide when that grouping happens.

— This choice defines how title embeddings are built before news is compared.
— `Local`: the app computes embeddings on device with `e5-small-multilang`.
— `Cloud`: embeddings come from added embedding configs and external providers.
— Switching strategy clears the old similarity cache and rebuilds feed clusters under the new mode.

— Scheduled summaries enable automatic digest generation by schedule.
— You can add several run times, for example morning and evening.
— Push notifications control notifications after a summary is created.
— For more reliable delivery, remove background work restrictions and allow app autostart.
— Show news in statistics defines how many items appear in the summary dashboard.
— This switch controls the “Recommended” badges on the subscriptions screen in Sources.\n— Recommendations are computed by comparing important news from your sources with each theme’s anchors.

— Article auto cleanup defines after how many days old articles are removed automatically.
— Clear articles removes the local feed content but keeps the sources.
— Clear embeddings resets vector data and similarity cache.
— Clear scheduled summaries removes stored scheduled summary history.
— Reset settings returns app preferences to their default values.
— In `Overwrite` mode there is no item-by-item merge.\n— After sync, only one side remains: local or cloud.\n— Which side wins is defined by the priority below.

— In `Merge` mode the app combines local and cloud state for each selected category.\n— If an item exists on at least one side, it is kept in the result.\n— This is a union of two states, not a hard replacement.

— In `Overwrite` mode, `Local` priority means Firebase is replaced with the current state of this device.\n— Remote state is not applied first.\n— After sync, local state is treated as the source of truth.

— In `Overwrite` mode, `Cloud` priority means this device first accepts the state from Firebase.\n— Local data for selected categories is replaced by cloud data.\n— After sync, cloud state is treated as the source of truth.

— Turning this on schedules background sync and immediately starts a sync now run.\n— It only applies to the categories selected below.\n— If API-key sync has no passphrase, that category is automatically disabled.

— This is the background cloud sync frequency in hours.\n— A shorter interval keeps devices aligned faster, but wakes background work more often.\n— Real delivery timing still depends on Android background limits.

— Includes the actual news sources and their technical parameters in sync.\n— Without this, another device will not receive newly added RSS, Telegram, or YouTube sources.\n— This does not sync article content by itself.
— Syncs subscription structure, folders, and topic groupings.\n— This preserves how your sources are organized, not just the raw source list.\n— Useful if you actively manage folders and themes.
— Syncs your saved articles across devices.\n— This helps you continue reading from the items you explicitly bookmarked.\n— It affects saved state, not the normal feed contents.

— Syncs app settings except secrets: language, theme, summary/feed behavior, scheduled summary, and more.\n— This is the main switch for moving app behavior across devices.\n— API keys are handled separately.

— Adds AI configs and API keys to sync.\n— Before upload to Firebase, keys are encrypted through PBKDF2 + AES-256-GCM and are never sent in plain text.\n— If no encryption passphrase is configured, the app automatically clears this option.

— This shows the time of the last successful synchronization.\n— If you see “never”, no full sync has completed successfully yet.\n— It is the quickest indicator of whether the cloud already has your current state.

— Adds news sources and their technical parameters to the backup file.\n— Without this, restore will not bring back the actual RSS, Telegram, or YouTube source list.\n— Useful when moving the content base to another device.
— Exports or imports groups, themes, and subscription structure.\n— This preserves organization logic, not only the raw list of sources.\n— Especially useful when folders are part of your workflow.
— Transfers your saved article list.\n— This prevents manually bookmarked items from being lost during migration.\n— It restores saved state, not the full feed history.
— Transfers app settings without secrets: language, theme, AI/feed/scheduled parameters, and similar preferences.\n— API keys are controlled by the separate option below.

— Adds provider configs and API keys to backup or import.\n— This requires the passphrase from which the app derives the encryption key through PBKDF2.\n— Without that passphrase, API keys cannot be encrypted safely or restored later.
— During import, selected local categories are fully replaced by the file contents.\n— The result keeps only the state from the backup.
— During import, each selected category keeps everything that exists either locally or in the file.\n— This is a merge of two states, not a full replacement.
— The app interface switches to Ukrainian: menus, buttons, dialogs, and help text.\n— It is applied globally through application locales.\n— It does not change the language of AI summaries.
— The app interface switches to English: menus, buttons, dialogs, and help text.\n— It applies across the whole app, not only Settings.\n— It does not define the language of AI responses.

— Generated summaries and AI answers should be written in Ukrainian even for sources in other languages.\n— This affects the summary screen, feed AI, and related flows.\n— Useful when you want one consistent result language regardless of input.

— Generated summaries and AI answers should be written in English regardless of source language.\n— Useful for international sources or when sharing results more broadly.\n— It does not change the interface language.
— The app follows the device light or dark theme.\n— This is the most natural mode if you do not want a separate SumUp appearance.\n— When the system theme changes, the app changes too.
— Forces a light appearance regardless of the system theme.\n— Useful for daytime reading or when you want a stable light UI.\n— System dark mode is ignored for SumUp.
— Forces a dark appearance regardless of the system theme.\n— Useful for evening reading or OLED screens.\n— System light mode no longer affects SumUp.

— This is one concrete cloud summary config: provider, model, and access key.\n— The top enabled config is tried first, so ordering matters.\n— Tapping opens editing, while the switch temporarily excludes the config without deleting it.

— This is one concrete embeddings config for similarity-related tasks.\n— These models are used for cloud deduplication, recommendations, and related vector workflows.\n— Order and enabled state decide which config the app tries first.

— Local strategy avoids external LLM providers for summaries.\n— It relies on extractive logic inside the app, so it does not spend API tokens.\n— Some flows such as follow-up questions are naturally more limited here.

— Cloud strategy sends prepared text directly to one of the available summary configs.\n— Quality is usually higher, but it consumes provider quota and tokens.\n— If the top config fails, the app can try other enabled keys.

— Adaptive strategy decides when local processing is enough and when compressed text should be sent to the cloud.\n— Short material may stay fully local, while longer content is extractively shrunk first.\n— This is the main mode for saving tokens without giving up cloud models entirely.

— Enables your own extra prompt on top of the app’s system instructions.\n— It changes style, emphasis, and tone, but does not remove service format rules.\n— Turning it off returns the app to the standard SumUp prompt only.

— Use this field to add custom preferences for summary style or AI answers.\n— It supplements the system prompt instead of replacing the technical response structure.\n— Overly strict or conflicting instructions can make results less stable.

— Caps how much text can be sent to the cloud for a single-article summary.\n— A smaller limit saves tokens and speeds responses up.\n— On long articles, some context is trimmed before the model call.

— Caps the total payload for comparing or summarizing a cluster of similar news.\n— Important when many sources describe the same event in long form.\n— If the limit is too small, the result may include fewer viewpoints.

— Caps how much one article may contribute to a cloud feed summary or scheduled digest.\n— This prevents one long item from consuming the whole request budget.\n— Especially useful for lengthy posts or articles with heavy body text.

— Caps the total text of one cluster inside larger cloud feed summaries.\n— This prevents one story with many duplicates from overwhelming the model.\n— Lowering it usually saves tokens faster than it hurts quality.

— This is the maximum payload for one cloud request overall.\n— If all selected content exceeds it, some context is reduced or cut before sending.\n— It is the main control for speed, cost, and stability in large summaries.

— If text is shorter than this threshold, adaptive mode may stay local and skip a cloud call.\n— This is the strongest token-saving rule for short content.\n— The threshold is measured in input characters.

— This threshold separates medium-sized texts from very long ones.\n— Between the lower threshold and this one, the app uses medium pre-compression before cloud processing.\n— Everything above it moves into the third, strongest compression range.

— This marks the third range: everything longer than the upper threshold gets the strongest compression.\n— There is no separate “to infinity” slider because this range always starts after the second threshold.\n— The actual compression percentage for this range is configured below.

— Defines how much text to keep in the first range before further processing.\n— A value of 0 means: use the standard local extractive sentence selection.\n— A higher percentage keeps more context but saves fewer tokens.

— Defines compression strength for medium texts between the lower and upper thresholds.\n— A lower percentage saves more tokens before the cloud call.\n— If it is too aggressive, important nuance may be lost.

— Defines compression strength for the longest texts above the upper threshold.\n— This is usually the smallest percentage because it cuts payload most aggressively.\n— It has the strongest impact on the cost of large summaries.
— Adds images and previews to feed cards when a source provides them.\n— This makes the feed richer visually, but can increase clutter and loading.\n— It does not directly change AI behavior.
— Shows a short text preview below the headline.\n— Helpful for quick scanning, but the feed becomes less compact.\n— It does not directly affect sources or summaries.

— This setting affects full-feed summarization and scheduled digests specifically, not the visual appearance of feed cards.\n— When it is enabled, the app tries to send the full article text to AI instead of a short annotation.\n— When it is disabled, the default input is the headline plus the short feed description, or only a small leading part of Telegram posts.

— Before building the feed, the app drops news with a low informativeness score.\n— That score is based on facts and numbers in the text, text length, view counts, and penalties for ad-like or clickbait wording.\n— The same threshold is also used before scheduled summaries are built.
— Local deduplication computes embeddings on device with `e5-small-multilang`.\n— After switching, the app clears the old similarity cache, rebuilds it, and rebuilds the feed.
— Cloud deduplication uses added embedding configs and external providers to compute embeddings.\n— After switching, the app also clears the old similarity cache and rebuilds the feed.

— Enables grouping of similar news into clusters.\n— News with no cluster match does not disappear: it stays as a separate feed item.\n— The thresholds below matter only while deduplication is enabled.

— After clusters are built, this hides items that did not reach the required number of similar news matches.\n— That threshold is controlled by the minimum similar count setting below.\n— If this switch is off, such single items still stay in the feed.

— Defines how similar local embeddings must be for news to be treated as the same story.\n— A higher threshold is stricter: only very close items are merged.\n— Changing it triggers similarity rebuild and feed refresh.

— The same threshold, but for cloud embeddings.\n— A higher value reduces accidental merges of different stories, but leaves more duplicates.\n— Changing it also rebuilds the similarity cache for current data.

— This is the minimum number of additional similar articles next to the main one.\n— A value of 1 means a cluster of at least 2 items, a value of 2 means at least 3.\n— It matters most together with the “hide single items” switch.

— Enables automatic summary generation on the chosen schedule.\n— The times below are normalized and stored as the worker’s run list.\n— Turning it off stops new scheduled summaries, but does not delete old history.
— After a scheduled summary is created, the app can send a push notification.\n— On Android 13+, notification permission is also required.\n— If permission is denied, the switch is turned back off.

— This is one concrete automatic summary run time.\n— Tapping edits the time, while the trash action removes the slot when more than one exists.\n— You can keep multiple runs per day, such as morning and evening.
— Adds one more time slot to the scheduled summary list.\n— The new slot is normalized together with the rest so the list stays ordered.\n— This is how you configure multiple digests per day.

— This reminder explains that scheduled summary delivery still depends on Android background work limits.\n— For better reliability, allow autostart and avoid aggressive battery restrictions.\n— Otherwise the system may delay or skip the worker run.

— Defines how many news items appear in the summary statistics and infographic.\n— It does not change whether a summary is generated, only how detailed the analytics block is.\n— Higher values make the dashboard richer but denser.

— Controls the “Recommended” badges on the subscriptions screen in Sources and whether recommendation logic is actively run.\n— When this switch is on, the app compares important news from your sources with each theme’s anchors.\n— When this switch is off, the theme list stays visible, but recommendations are not recalculated and the badges are hidden.

— Defines after how many hours older articles are automatically removed from local storage.\n— It does not touch sources or subscriptions.\n— Lower values save space, but reduce local history for later processing.
— Completely clears locally stored articles and current feed contents.\n— Sources, groups, and settings remain intact.\n— The feed fills again only after sources refresh.

— Resets embeddings and similarity cache used for deduplication and related tasks.\n— It also invalidates the current dedup runtime state.\n— Useful when you want to force a full similarity rebuild from scratch.
— Deletes stored scheduled summary history.\n— It does not disable the schedule and does not affect sources.\n— New scheduled summaries will continue appearing on future runs.

— Restores `UserSettings()` default values.\n— It also reapplies the default app language and refreshes scheduled summary configuration.\n— This does not delete sources or API configs, but it resets app behavior back to default.
